So next we have item 1.03, which is the FY 2025 Office of Auditor General Annual Report. So now I call on General Koh and Deputy General Danielle Moore for item 1.03.

Thank you, Ryan, and good afternoon, everyone, and happy new year. Welcome to the first of the year Audit Committee meeting. And today we have a pretty brief agenda, so we are very happy to be able to spotlight our accomplishment and achievement for the past fiscal year.

So with that, first of all, I would like to thank all the Audit Committee members and the chairs for the continued support for the OAG work. And I also want to express my appreciation to all the OAG members. As you all know, we try to bring the full team each time for the audit committee meetings so that you can see kind of who is actually working behind of all the audit reports.

And we have worked very hard to complete our audits, inquiries, and all the training programs. It truly takes a team effort to accomplish the task that's delegated to us by the school board and the audit committee. And also, I would like to give a thank you to our hourly auditor, Mukta, and he cannot be with us today, but he is one of the primary authors of the annual report.

So I would like to give him the, you know, thank you for that. And logistically, after today's presentation, this annual report will be presented to the school board on June 23rd. So it's a little bit later.

And it is because that the chairs would like to combine the annual report discussion together with the fiscal year 27 audit topics discussion. So it will be around that time. And we can talk more if that time needs to be adjusted or what.

So for today, within this annual report, we highlight our accomplishments over the past year over mainly our four pillars of work. That's how we normally call them. The first one is listed on the transmittal letter, and thank you, Claire, if you can just stay at the…yes, that would be great.

So the first area is risk assessment. Risk assessment A is how we identify and select audit topics. The second pillar is internal audit, meaning our core function, the bread and butter, or in the Asian way, I will call it rice and noodle.

So what we mainly do for the comfort food, I mean for the main thing for internal audit. And then the C area is fraud, waste, and abuse hotline. So here is ensuring when things will not quite go the right way, such as when there are concerns for misuse of funds, stakeholders have a tip line to raise that concern to OAG, Office of Auditor General.

We also do a lot of outreach and education work as well. So because we know, even though OAG has been doing a lot of excellent work, but if we do not communicate it actively with our staff or community, it means that we have not done that.

So together, these four pillars create a holistic approach for my office to review FCPS processes for effectiveness, efficiency, and to ensure accountability to all the Fairfax County community members.

And for those of you who are watching this meeting this afternoon, the Office of Auditor General reports directly to the school board, and I'm going to page one of this report, as well as the Audit Committee. As many of you know that independence is really essential for the success of the office.

So page one of this report highlight that we report to the school board via the Audit Committee, who is the meeting today. And then on this page, we also highlight the audit committee charter according to the governance manual.

And pages two and three of this report continue to outline the policy 1105, which is the Auditor General Authority. And it, again, emphasized the importance of independence, as well as on this page, under item E, it talks about audit standard and ethics.

So for audit standard, we follow the government accountability office, they publish the, I bring this with me, the government auditing standard, and we call this as the yellow book. And to me, sometimes a physical copy always tell a little bit more.

And this is the standard that the federal agency follow, as well as many state and local audit organizations follow as well. So OAG follow the standard. And then moving on on page 4, it talks more about our mission, and I have already outlined that in the beginning, is that our office is to conduct independent assessment on all the ongoing FCPS processes, and to ensure that they are working effectively, efficiently, and be accountable to our community members.

And then on this page, we outline many of the OAG value that we measure our success against. if we can go down a little bit more. So there's a table here where we were able to get some of the benchmarking from the Council of Great City Schools.

And the data that we got is quite recent, is as of 2024 to 2025. So when you looked at the different indicators here, you can see that that OAG operate is at a more effective and efficient level compared to generally the other school districts.

And then also we are very glad to report that we were able to complete 100% of our audit plan and then we were able to have management accepted 100% of the recommendations. So here I would like to highlight as I mentioned we are independent but at the same time we have a very collaborative approach working with management so we are very grateful that the recommendations were fully accepted.

So moving on, on the page five in the beginning, we also conducted a survey after each audit with our audit clients, meaning with management. We asked questions based upon the eight different areas that, as you can see on the screen, such as if it is timely being announced about the audit is coming up, do we have an effective process, do you believe that the auditors contain sufficient knowledge?
So we aim at getting a higher than 90% of yes to these questions. And in fiscal year 25, we exceeded that indicator to receive more than 90% on all the indicators that we try to measure.

And then moving on, we have some other OAG achievements on our report cards as well. And here, there are a lot of wording here. We will go through each one of them in more details in a little bit. But for here I just want to highlight two things in the meantime.

One is that every three years, OAG will also be audited. So as a matter of fact, later this month we will have an external peer review team coming to look at how OAG is doing our audit according to the government auditing standard.
So we will be presenting the result in the next audit committee meeting in March. Then I also want to highlight that all our team members have the required certifications in doing what we do.

We have certified public accountants, we have certified internal auditor, fraud examiner, as well as information system auditors. Even though it sounds like a lot of alphabets, but I really want to highlight that because it added the credentials to what we do so that the community members can rely on our report.

performance audits and 14 business process audits as it relates to the six performance audits the first audit is the procurement process audit so the scope of this audit covered procurement processes administered by the office of procurement services and the vendor review process administered in collaboration with the office of cyber security as well as the technology architecture and and assessment section.

Some of the findings from this audit include an alignment of policies, regulations, and guidance regarding the vendor approval process, operational inefficiencies in vendor communication and review processes that impact the vendor solicitation, excuse me, and lack of key performance indicators.

Our second audit is the student disciplinary process audit, and this audit actually was exempt from disclosure, so we won't discuss those results in the open session. The third audit is the critical process review, and this is for hiring.

So during this audit, we did an evaluation of the key hiring processes. Some of the challenges noted included the design of the hiring and onboarding processes that may lead to inconsistent application of hiring practices, loss of interest from applicants, and data silos that disrupt workflows.

Our fourth audit is the construction and renovation contracting process audit. So the scope of this audit included the FCPS Capital Improvement Program projects that were funded for construction in the 2019, the 2021, and the 2023 bond referendums.

We also looked at key processes and controls related to the procurement, contract monitoring, change orders, contract invoicing, and contract closeout. Some of the findings noted included instances of noncompliance with project contract terms and the design and construction manual.

And there were several areas where improvements could be made in the FCPS construction monitoring practices, policies and guidelines that required an update. For our next set of audits, these audits are mainly our audits that are school related.

Since we are a school division, that's kind of our bread and butter. We have three different types of school related audits. Those include the local school activity funds audit, continuous monitoring and our business process audit.

So in FY25, we completed the Local School Activity Funds audit for year ending June 30th, 2025. And I like to note that this audit is one of those audits that are required by the Virginia Code. So we look at this, we do this audit every year.

So Local School Activity Funds are collected from students and parents, and they're to be used for the purpose in which they were collected. So this includes student fees, activity fees, and maybe something like parking fees. During our audit, the OAG did not have any findings, but we did have three observations related to compliance.

First observation was related to compliance with regulations. The second observation was related to cash receipts and the internal control environment. And the third observation, excuse me, was related to the deposit date control weakness related to the Great Plains accounting system.
So basically overall, out of this audit, we audited a total of 202 sites. We noted exceptions of noncompliance with regulations in 73 sites. And then we had no exceptions at the remaining 129 sites.

And I would like to note the individual exceptions occur that the site level did not impact the cash balance at the year end. And there were no material effect to FCPS as a division. Our other audit we conducted was the continuous monitoring.

This is, we do quarterly reviews of unusual transactions for both appropriated and local school activity funds transactions. The local school activity fund transactions, any exceptions noted will be included in our local school activities funds audit.

So it's kind of like what we use as our sample for local school activity funds. As well as any appropriated transactions or exceptions that we know that we use that to determine if we need to conduct a business process review audit.
So as far as the continuous monitoring for FY25, Out of the 202 sites, 103 sites had no exceptions noted. 55 sites had exceptions noted in three or fewer areas.

44 sites did not have any transactions that appeared in our sample. And I would also like to note that OAG did quarterly site visits at 68 sites. In our last set of audits, our business process audits, we conducted 14 business process audits in FY25, which included 13 schools and one department.

So the business process audits are a deeper dive. These are ad hoc audits that are a deeper dive. We usually conduct these audits due to change and management like the finance tech or the principal. Also based on the outcome of any continuous monitoring and other areas that are deemed necessary.

Mainly the findings related to the business process audits are the purchasing process, timeliness of payments, also the timeliness of completing bank reconciliations and the non-bank reconciliations, which may be your FMR, your financial management report.

Also, we have findings related to outstanding deposits and the sufficiency of documentation. And I would like to note that for these audits, we require a management response for any risk level, moderate or higher, so that would be a moderate or a high risk finding.

And we do follow up on those in a quarterly basis. As well as we follow up on all of the findings for our performance audits, which like I mentioned is done on a quarterly basis and we report out to the Audit Committee. And Monya will be talking a little bit later about that.

But as of FY25, OAG did note that we had 45 new recommendations for the audit performed and reported 30 of those recommendations closed. and as of July 31, 29 recommendations from the current and prior years remain outstanding.

And so some of those outstanding recommendations were related to the FY25 Food and Nutritional Services Audit, the FY20, I'm excuse me, FY24 Food and Nutrition Services Audit, the FY25 Procurement Process Audit, FY25 Critical Process Review for Hiring, and the FY25 Construction and Renovation Contracting Process Audit.
